criterion: Preserve requested facts, constraints, code behavior and language with no new material per-prompt regression versus strict. Different token IDs alone are not failure.

binding_finding.requested_scope: Practical INT4, W8A8 and BF16 tradeoffs, explicitly distinguishing memory capacity, bandwidth and native arithmetic support.
binding_finding.candidate_claim: AMD RX 7000: Limited or no native INT8 matrix multiplication support in consumer drivers. Often falls back to FP16 emulation, negating speed gains.
binding_finding.strict_comparison: Strict says RDNA3 has some INT8 support but its software stack is immature. It does not introduce the same absent-native-support/FP16-emulation explanation for AMD.
binding_finding.assessment: The candidate conflates framework/kernel availability with native arithmetic capability in the very distinction requested. RDNA3 provides native IU8 WMMA, and AMD demonstrates the supported HIP compiler path on Radeon RX 7900 XTX. Presenting native INT8 support as absent or driver-emulated is materially misleading.
binding_finding.qualification: The source establishes native instructions and a supported HIP path. It does not measure fallback prevalence across all libraries; this review does not claim to have disproved a frequency statistic experimentally.

primary_source.title: How to accelerate AI applications on RDNA 3 using WMMA
primary_source.support: Documents IU8/BF16/FP16 WMMA intrinsics, HIP/ROCm support and an RX 7900 XTX implementation.
